reference.title: Benefits of 2FA
reference.shortdesc: MFA concepts, authentication factors, and how MFA protects you against phishing and unauthorized account access.

section.title: Authentication Factors
section.p: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) requires combining two or more independent credentials from different verification categories:

ul.li: Something you know: Information you memorize, such as your NC State Unity ID password or a PIN.
Something you have: A physical device in your possession, such as a smartphone running the Duo Mobile app or a hardware security token.
Something you are: A biometric trait, such as a fingerprint or facial recognition scan.
Blocks phishing and password leaks: Even if cyber actors steal your password through phishing or a data breach, they still cannot sign in without your second authentication factor.
Reduces account compromise: According to CISA, enabling MFA makes your accounts 99 percent less likely to be hacked.
Alerts you to suspicious login attempts: Receiving an unexpected Duo prompt warns you immediately that someone has your password so you can deny the request and change your password.
